issues.description: StockIngredient getter name mismatch: the template defines StockIngredient.getIngredientName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient in the template calls getIngredientName(); the solution defines StockIngredient.getName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient in the solution calls getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify exact getter names. This identifier naming inconsistency can confuse students comparing template and solution or following guidance that expects a specific getter name.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent getter name for StockIngredient.name across template, solution, and the problem statement. Prefer the conventional getName(): rename the template method getIngredientName() to getName(), update all calls in template (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to use getName(), and clarify in the problem statement that getters should follow the standard getFieldName() naming (e.g., getName()). Alternatively, change the solution to use getIngredientName() and update its references—pick one naming convention and apply it everywhere so students are not confused.

issues.description: Concept: the getter for the StockIngredient.name field. Problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify exact method names. In the template repository, the getter is named getIngredientName() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) and Stock.findStockIngredient() in the template calls getIngredientName(). In the solution repository the getter is named getName() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getName(). This identifier-name mismatch for the same conceptual element (the name getter of StockIngredient) can confuse students about the expected getter name and cause friction when reading the template, tests, and solution or when trying to match method names expected by tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across all artifacts. Recommended: use getName(). Change the template's StockIngredient.getIngredientName() to getName() and update all calls (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to use getName(). Also update the problem statement to explicitly request conventional getter names (e.g., "provide getters named getX() for private fields, e.g., getName() for a name field") so students know the expected identifier convention.
